newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia subversion trials to start this month.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia subversion trials to start this month.

text.p: Indonesian prosecutors submitted documents to two courts on Monday listing charges of subversion against a labour leader and nine left-wing activists and the trials should begin in two weeks, officials and lawyers said.

Independent labour leader Muchtar Pakpahan and nine senior members of the left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD) were arrested within days of riots in Jakarta on July 27 and charged with subversion in connection with the violence.
Subversion carries the death penalty in Indonesia.

Cherry Usman, spokesman for the South Jakarta State Court, said prosecutors submitted the 700-page, 15 cm (six inch) thick documents on Pakpahan as well as Petrus Haryanto and Kenbudha Kusumandaru, two PRD activists.
"They are all subversion cases," Usman told Reuters, adding there would be three separate cases in the South Jakarta State Court.
The official Antara news agency later reported that subversion charges against two other activists, Putut Ariyantoko and Victor da Costa, would be heard in Kusumandaru's case.

Usman said the timing of the trial would depend on the judges. Pakpahan's lawyer Luftie Hakim told Reuters he expected to receive this week a copy of the dossier on his client and to soon be notified of a date for the trial.
"The trial could start as soon as 10 days after this," he said. Pakpahan has been in custody since he was arrested.

Haryanto and Kusumandaru were part of a group of PRD leaders, including chairman Budiman Sudjatmiko, arrested after they were blamed by the government for instigating riots in July in which at least five people died. The riots were the worst in the capital for more than 20 years.
Officials at the Central Jakarta State Court said documents for three seperate cases involving five other PRD leaders had been lodged there on Monday.
Antara said Sudjatmiko and Garda Sembiring would be tried in separate hearings while Jakobus Eko, Damianus Pranowo and Suroso would be tried simultaneously in a third hearing.

"It is hoped that in the middle of December, the trials of those accused of subversive actions can start," Antara quoted the chief judge of the Central Jakarta State Court, I Gde Sukarata, as saying after receiving the dossiers.
The July riots erupted after police raided the headquarters of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) and evicted supporters of ousted PDI leader Megawati Sukarnoputri.
Megawati, the daughter of late founding president Sukarno, was removed by a government-backed PDI faction in June.
Authorities have said left-wing groups modelled on the banned communist party took advantage of the PDI rift to instigate riots and promote hatred against the government.
Pakpahan is not a member of the PRD but was sentenced to three years jail in 1994 for sparking rioting in the North Sumatran city of Medan in April that year.

On appeal, he had his sentence first raised to four years before it was quashed by the Supreme Court in September 1995. Last month, the Supreme Court re-imposed the original sentence after reviewing its earlier decision.
